notes:
ACCESS: probe.fetch() (curl_cffi fingerprint rotation) reached every page and the site's own PLP endpoint without a challenge; occasional transient 'TLS connect error (curl 35)' on a single fingerprint was retried on a different profile. ROBOTS: https://www.hkliving.com/robots.txt was requested FIRST and is GENUINELY ABSENT - HTTP 404 with a zero-length body and no content-type, reproduced on www.hkliving.com, the apex hkliving.com (301 -> www), plain http://, the locale path /en/robots.txt, and with a cache-busting query string, on three separate impersonation profiles. hkliving.nl 301-redirects to the same www.hkliving.com host, and shop.hkliving.com does not resolve (DNSError), so there is no second storefront host with its own robots file. A missing robots.txt is not a robots exclusion: NOTHING is declared about anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-User anywhere, no Disallow exists, and no Crawl-delay is declared - I nevertheless kept probe.py's 2s per-host pacing plus a further 2s between the page fetch and its payload call. TREE: taken from the site's OWN rendered mega-menu, not guessed. The homepage header menu and the /products/ category index both render the complete tree as plain anchors; both were fetched and enumerated and they agree exactly. HKliving is Umbraco-backed (VWA Digital Agency) and its department set is: Sofas (6 children), Furniture (7), Kitchen (13), Textile (6), Lighting (6), Accessories (10), Outdoor (3), Art, Brand kit, Add ons - 10 departments and 51 leaves. Add ons and Brand kit render no product grid at all (no #__CategoryId hidden input, no article list) and are B2B pages, not listings. THERE IS NO BATHROOM / BADKAMER / SANITAIR DEPARTMENT AND NO BATHROOM LEAF ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. QTY: the PLP is client-rendered (the server HTML ships only empty
placeholders), so I used the storefront's own product API - the exact one the PLP itself renders from. products-js-bundle.js shows VWA.filter.reloadProducts() POSTing to /umbraco/surface/AsyncContentSurface/Index?categoryId=<__CategoryId>&renderPath=Catalog&doGroupProducts=1 with the view list [ArticleList, ActiveFilters, FilterOptions, Pager]; main-js-bundle.js shows VWA.utils.requestApi sending it as JSON with headers PwaDisableCache:1 and RequestVerificationToken taken from the page's hidden __RequestVerificationToken. I replayed exactly that call in-session (page GET first, so the antiforgery cookie/token pair and the categoryId come from the node's own HTML) and read the site's own rendered header N. EQUIVALENCE PROVED three ways over a 61-node sweep of every department and every leaf: (1) on every node whose total is at or below the 16-per-page page size, totalcount equals the number of
tiles the API returned exactly - Bath mats 7/7, Towels & robes 6/6, Clocks 7/7, Stools 7/7, Benches 9/9, Dining chairs 10/10, Artist ceramics 10/10, Vint couch 11/11, Table lamps 12/12, Lamp bases 13/13, Dining tables 13/13, Fauteuils 14/14, Shell ceramics 8/8, Flowerpots 8/8, Outdoor accessories 4/4, Wall lamps 1/1, Clothing racks 1/1; (2) the returned Pager agrees with ceil(totalcount/16) on every multi-page node - Accessories 215 -> 14 pages, Kitchen 499 -> 32, Tableware 370 -> 24, 70s ceramics 312 -> 20, Mugs & cups 154 -> 10, Kitchen accessories 132 -> 9, Textile 126 -> 8, Bowls 102 and Serveware 103 -> 7, Furniture 109 -> 7 - so totalcount is a true paginated total and not a page-size artifact; (3) children sum exactly to their parent on three departments - Textile 7+5+63+43+6+2 = 126 = Textile's own 126, Sofas 1+9+8+4+11+18 = 51 = 51, Outdoor 4+18+2 = 24 = 24. Counts discriminate hard: 1 to 499 across 59 listing nodes, no site-wide constant. Each node's identity was verified from its own breadcrumb
    and its

    before its count was read (e.g. Bath mats -> crumb Home / All Products / Textile / Bath mats, h2 'Bath mats', categoryId 57730). VERIFICATION OF ABSENCE: (a) the full 61-node tree contains no bathroom node; (b) the homepage and /products/ HTML contain ZERO occurrences of badkamer, sanitair, shower, douche, toilet, wc, basin, wastafel, soap or zeep, and the only 'bath'/'towel' hits are the two Textile leaves above; (c) I swept all 59 listing nodes through the API and regex-scanned the 700 returned product titles for bath|shower|douche|badkamer|toilet|wc|basin|sink|soap|zeep|toothbrush|towel|robe|mirror|spiegel|sanitair|faucet|tap|bidet|vanity|caddy|dispenser - the ONLY hits are the 7 textile bath mats, the 6 towels/robes, the 15 decorative mirrors in Accessories > Mirrors, four 'Mirror block' coffee tables in Furniture > Side tables (mirrored-glass tables, not mirrors), and five 'tea towel' kitchen linens. HKliving is a wholesale interiors brand: it sells no sanitaryware, no taps, no baths, no showers, no WCs, no bathroom furniture, no bathroom storage, no bathroom mirrors and no bathroom accessories (no soap dispenser, no toothbrush holder, no toilet-roll holder, no towel rail). NEAREST MISSES CHECKED AND REJECTED: Accessories > Home fragrances (19) is candles/diffusers, not rule-13 soap accessories; Kitchen > Kitchen accessories (132) was scanned and is kitchen tools/storage with no soap dispenser or bathroom item; Furniture > Cabinets & shelves (28) is living-room cabinets and shelving with no vanity or bathroom unit - and it is in any case already in Furniture.xlsx as 'Cabinets & Shelves'. DEDUP: dedup.already_extracted() was run on every candidate and every review URL. Accessories > Mirrors is already in Final.xlsx (Home Decor pass) as 'Mirrors' and Furniture > Cabinets & shelves is already in Furniture.xlsx as 'Cabinets & Shelves' (OPTION 1 - it stays in Furniture); Bath mats and Towels & robes are not in the index and are excluded on their own merits as Textile, not by dedup. EXCLUDED: Art, Brand kit, Add ons, Collections/Collaborations/Catalogues pages (rule 25 - collection and promotional pages, and they carry no product grid). VERDICT: NO BATHROOM FOUND (rule 36) - a genuine catalogue absence, not a dedup artifact and not an access failure.
